Check the thing the checks are measured against, not just the thing being measured. #81 had four rounds of hardening on src and zero on the root src was compared to.

A check that cannot fail where it runs is worse than no check: it occupies a slot, and it teaches readers that red means environment. Before shipping a fix, ask where it will run and whether it can fail there.
Fixing one copy of duplicated logic and watching tests pass proves nothing. #91 fixed scanner.ts, output did not change, and three new tests went green against the copy nobody calls.
Read the open issues for the assumption you are about to encode. #77 documented the projectRoot/harnessRoot divergence before I shipped code depending on projectRoot.
A guard is only as good as its view of the input. Before trusting one, measure how much of the file it can actually see.
Do not close an issue from a list. Re-verify against the code — a stale-list entry closed #69 would have buried nine live defects.
When a fix needs an independent witness, pick one the implementation cannot influence: a real parser, a second tool, the artifact a reader opens.

An SC that asserts a name appears in a file cannot see a false premise in the design decision above it. #139: twelve such SCs across four phases, all green, while every Octokit call in the repo threw at construction. Pair existence SCs with one that makes a call.

items: Four merges, all the same shape: a check whose phase has nothing to do with the phase that can act on it. #261 (92a9b55c) — the evidence pre-validation reading was produced only inside runScopePreflights, so on a LIGHT run nothing produced it and the verify gate refused on a reading never taken. #264 (f67d38f9) — the reading was taken in the wrong directory under worktree isolation and never re-taken when the run healed; it now carries takenAt and reads EVIDENCE_CWD. #267 (91eb044c) — the multi-worktree collector assembled into PROJECT_ROOT, which sits on main, which the commit step refuses; run wf_19f7def7-1bf produced a complete implementation and could not commit a line of it, leaving 907 unreviewed lines staged on main. #269 (c73d566b) — an AC carrying threshold >= 1 passed Discovery, skipped scope, and was first validated by the commit recorder four phases later, so a whole implementation was produced against a criterion nobody could measure.

#269's inlined copy of ACSchema is held honest by a 28-case bidirectional parity matrix (the #224 pattern): every case runs through both the copy and the real schema and fails on disagreement in EITHER direction. It caught the copy twice drifting STRICTER than the schema — refusing an empty id and a missing evidence field that ACSchema accepts. A copy stricter than its referent refuses valid runs and nothing downstream ever contradicts it.

A section documenting a deliberate divergence was written on a wrong premise — I believed evidence was required; EvidenceSchema is .nullable().optional() at gates/schema.ts:45. Converted into a test that fires if the premise ever becomes true, rather than deleted.

A background security review found three real defects in my own merged-pending #269 work: a fail-open empty-array return for a non-array AC list, a validator differential (base-shape rules missing from the copy), and a control misfire (refusal text asserting a commit state that is false on the verify-regression path, where runDiscovery runs a second time). Two more defects found in the same run and filed rather than fixed. #271 extended: the pre-validator classified #273's AC-1 as broken because grep -c exits 1 on zero matches, and AC-1's threshold is == 0 — so a zero-count AC is reported healthy while the bug exists and broken the moment it is fixed. tryFixGrepExitCode declines to help because it skips piped commands, and a count-style grep is almost always piped. #280: the ship gate reads a verify-era evidencePrevalidation block and never re-measures, which is my own #264 fix stopping one phase short — third instance in that family.

#277 filed: an AC with no recorded evidence passes verify for 11 of 13 EVIDENCE_METHOD_TYPES. evidence-method-executed covers only COMMAND/command; threshold-crosscheck skips any AC lacking evidence. The component whose job is to catch that — the B2 Evidence Validator — is LIGHT-gated off and has never run here, and when it does run it emits WARN rather than FAIL.

#274 corrected upward: LIGHT disables ELEVEN subsystems, not five. #271 fixed and merged (0a42a945). A grep that selected nothing was classified broken, and for a zero-count AC that is exactly when the work succeeds: grep -c prints 0 and exits 1, threshold == 0 is satisfied iff the count is 0, so the AC read healthy while the bug existed and broken the moment it was fixed. Replaced the || true auto-fix with grep's documented contract — exit 1 is no-match, exit >1 is an error — which is strictly narrower, because the wrapper laundered exit 2 as well. Only the last pipeline stage is consulted, or any command could buy amnesty by mentioning grep. Three existing tests asserted the removed wrapper and were INVERTED rather than deleted. Mutations: classification forced back to exit status 3 of 8 red; last-stage restriction dropped 1 of 8.

#285 filed, and it is the first concrete PROVEN cost of #274 rather than an argument from absence. workflows/ship.js:1808-1813 tells an agent to heal a tests-pass failure by running record-suite-measurement.ts with --result and --project; the script accepts only state, sha and failures, and --failures is required and never passed. COMP-4 flagged #273's run for modifying two specs without a hash update. session.summary: Four defects merged, all one shape: a check positioned in a phase that cannot act on it (#261, #264, #267, #269). Two of the four were introduced by the fix for the one above them, which is why the lesson is recorded as a cross-cutting table rather than four entries. The session then turned from fixing instances to finding the class: #273 proves six phase-ordering checks assert on comments — gutting the PR step while leaving its comment in place leaves all six green against a harness with zero pr-upsert call sites — and #274 proves pages:{} forces every rungate self-run to LIGHT, so the scope gate, Quinn local, Quinn verify, prove and the remote pre-flight have never executed on this repo. DailyBriefDashboard configures 18 pages and will enter all five on its first run. The Phase C chain is now measured end to end: DDB's test-container rule requires container config, which triggers #254, which is blocked by #273. Then #273's own ship run failed, and the failure paid for itself: it exposed #279, a collect step that dropped 926 lines of correct work and exited 0 because its empty-collection guard counted worktrees instead of files. Fixed and merged the same session. Two further defects filed from the same run (#271 extended, #280), and #274's count corrected from five never-executed subsystems to eleven. Seven issues closed in the end: the original four, plus #279, #271 and #273 — the last three all cleared from the wreckage of a single failed ship run, which is the best argument this session produced for running the pipeline against itself rather than reasoning about it. LATER IN THE SAME SESSION: #276 merged as d0d10478 after independent verification — the new marked block executed over all four reachable states, the full suite re-run from the worktree rather than from /tmp (5132 pass / 0 fail / 5299 tests), and the run's one self-healed regression triaged rather than accepted: its AC selector `--grep 'mutation'` matched 0 tests because the tests are named `MUTANT:`, which is #217 observed live and is now argued there as a promotion. SC-673..678 were checked for collision before merge, because #194's proposed SC-640..644 had collided with five live criteria. Then #254 was attempted and could not be shipped: prior-branch detection nominates a #228 rescue branch marked 'do not merge' and ship.js:2931 makes it the push target, a non-fast-forward by ancestry. #254 is therefore re-chained behind #185. Two issues filed from measurement rather than suspicion: #287, COMP-4 is satisfied by running shasum on ANY file — its declared checkMethod in test/compliance-tests.json requires Bash shasum AND an Edit to the hash constant, and the implementation is an OR over bashes that never reads data.edits at all, so the one thing it exists to verify is the one thing unchecked; and #288, a run's artefacts are not attributable to it — WORK_DIR is keyed by slug so a failed run's workflow-state.json, rook-findings.json and worktree-groups.json survive into the next run of the same issue, and priorWork is passed to initWorkflow at ship.js:1623, is absent from InitWorkflowInput, is never written, and is read by nothing. #288 was found by being fooled by it: a stale state file at phase VERIFY was mistaken for the live run and a healthy run was stopped on that misreading. Backlog re-triage answered the standing question — three issues most likely to have gone stale (#244, #263, #217) were checked against source and ALL THREE are live, so the growth from 43 to 51 open is the pipeline finding real defects, not drift; the lever is the critical path, not pruning. Housekeeping measured and deliberately NOT filed to avoid backlog noise: 122 worktrees occupy 891M of a 1.1G repo, 63 hold uncommitted trees, but #228 preservation is working (196 worktree-* branches, sampled dirty worktrees all have one), so this is cleanup with no correctness consequence and no retention policy. END OF SESSION 38: the Phase C chain was cleared three links at a time. #185 merged e313187f, #254 merged 333a199e on its sixth attempt, and #215 is in flight. Two defects were found by checking the harness's own output rather than trusting it, and both are now recorded rather than merely fixed. First, run wf_216bff9a-c13 passed its verify gate on commit 4122cddf and left that commit UNPUSHED — PR #290 carried 5abf0369, the earlier tree, which differs on the issue's own subject: the library emitted mergedIntoBase while both consumers read isMerged, so squash detection was wired to nothing and no branch could ever be reusable. Fail-closed, so nothing unsafe, but the positive control passed only against a shape the library cannot produce. Pushed by hand before merging; measured evidence added to #213, which already names that outcome. Second, mergedIntoBase's docblock promised fail-closed and nothing could falsify it — changing its TREE_OID guard to return true left 0 of 44 red, because the only unmeasured test removes the base and returns null from the function's first line without ever reaching the guard. git merge-tree --write-tree exits 1 for an unusable ref exactly as it does for a real conflict, so the error arrives looking like an answer. Now SC-687, and the same mutation is 2 of 47 red. Three stale PRs were closed rather than merged (#278, #207, #187): each had fallen far enough behind main that merging would have deleted 1979, 20069 and 22387 lines respectively — merge-ready landmines, branches and issues left intact. SESSION 39: the blocker under #274 turned out to be the harness, not the issue. Three #274 runs produced 4,855 lines and landed none; every refusal was correct and every cause was ours. #296 fixed it and is merged. Five defects were found by measuring rather than reading, and each is filed with the measurement attached. #294 is the sharpest: tests-pass is gated on dev.testCmd while the test baseline reads test.command — same file, same fact, two key names — and rungate and DDB are exactly complementary, so neither project exercises both. Observed two-sided with one planted state and two projectRoots: at rungate the check passes having made ZERO expect() calls, at DDB the identical state fails at the assertion. #224's mutation-proven binding has therefore never been REACHED on this repo — the function can fail, nothing proves the gate calls it. #295 came out of an agent's findings array and was nearly lost with its run: prevalidationViolations reads a top-level reading.broken that no writer produces, so every pre-validation refusal is unable to name which AC is broken. #302 came from the automated push review, not from Rook, which returned PASS on the same branch — the conformity allowlist ratchet enforces staleness but not growth. On #302 I first claimed #296 was shipping a new bypass, then checked main and found the opposite: `if (unconstrained)` already precedes every claim check, so a single-worktree run could always write any file, and #296 NARROWS that. Corrected on the PR before merging rather than after. #287's COMP-4 was executed rather than read: it scores `echo SPEC_HASH` as FOLLOWED and scores an agent that actually edits the constant as IGNORED — satisfiable by typing the word, not by doing the work.
